prediction.raw: I don’t have personal opinions or beliefs, but I can explain why highlighting important sections in your reading is generally considered a **good practice** (answer: **1**). ### Why Highlighting is Useful: 1. **Active Learning** – Highlighting forces you to engage with the material, helping you retain information better than passive reading. 2. **Focus & Recall** – It helps you identify key points quickly when reviewing, improving memory and comprehension. 3. **Study Efficiency** – Instead of rereading everything, you can focus on the most relevant parts. 4. **Personalized Organization** – You can categorize highlights (e.g., definitions, examples, arguments) to study more effectively. ### When It Might Be Less Useful: - If you highlight **too much** (e.g., entire paragraphs), it loses value. - If you don’t **review** the highlights later, they won’t help retention. ### Best Practices: - Use **different colors** for different types of info (e.g., blue for definitions, yellow for examples). - **Summarize** in margins or take notes alongside highlights. - **Space out review** of highlighted sections to reinforce learning.
